item.title: Trump announces Russian diesel deal weeks after signing sweeping sanctions law
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he was expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons “immediately thereafter.” Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.

Trump’s shocking announcement comes after he signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law last month that aimed at clamping down on Russia’s oil and gas revenues that fuel its war against Ukraine.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it “a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners," according to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington.

Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to try to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

“I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,” Zelenskyy said.

Trump's move casts doubt on the likelihood of the White House imposing sanctions on Russia this month, given that a bipartisan law passed by Congress directs the administration to target the top importers of Russian oil and gas.

Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., who co-sponsored the Russian sanctions law, slammed it as a “poorly concealed attempt to mitigate the havoc caused by Trump’s illegal war in Iran.”

“The President’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel is an embarrassment and makes us complicit in Putin’s war against Ukraine," he said in a statement.

Trump, in his announcement, did not address the sanctions or Russia’s war but said, “Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority.”

Trump said later as he left the White House for a campaign rally that he was thankful for the deal. "I want to thank President Putin. To be honest with you, we have massive amounts of oil coming into our country, and it’s diesel, which is what we want. So, thank you," Trump said. He did not answer shouted questions about the criticism from Zelenskyy.

Washington and Moscow offer few details on deal

The White House did not immediately respond to questions about who was paying for the diesel from Russia and when the fuel being supplied under the agreement would become available. It also did not clarify whether subsequent supplies of Russian diesel set to come next month would be supplied prior to Election Day on Nov. 3.

Gas prices globally have surged as the war in Iran upends the energy sector. While diesel future prices dipped on the news on Friday, the national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. remained high at $6.28, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on Sept. 22.

A statement from Putin, released by the Kremlin on Friday, said that during their call he and Trump dedicated “significant attention to the prospects of resolving the Ukrainian crisis” and also discussed “the situation around Iran and various aspects of bilateral relations.”

Russia “confirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and global markets,” Putin said. “I am confident that this will have a positive impact on the entire global economy.”

The two leaders agreed to continue contacts, Putin said in the statement.

Trump and Putin's deal draws immediate backlash

Zelenskyy, in a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, said Russia would repay it “with further terror and perfidy.” He cast it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged.

“It plays into Russia’s hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.

Blumenthal, in his scathing statement, invoked the memory of Sen. Lindsey Graham, a Trump ally and Russia hawk, for whom the sanctions law is named after.

“This agreement with a murdering dictator is a stain on our nation’s character, an insult to Lindsey Graham’s memory, and directly contrary to Congress’s intent in our bipartisan sanctions bill," he said.

Rep. Don Beyer, the senior House Democrat on the Joint Economic Committee, called Trump’s announcement “infuriating.”

“This is what we warned anyone who would listen: Trump isn’t the slightest bit trustworthy when it comes to Russia,” Beyer said in a statement on X.

The law Trump signed last month envisions sanctions on Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers and bans all new U.S. investment in Russia and the handling of sovereign debt.

It also directed Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia’s natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.

The U.S. has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned the imports because of Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Treasury Department moves to ease diesel sanctions for six months

Shortly after Trump made the announcement, the Treasury Department said it was immediately issuing a temporary license allowing Russian diesel to be supplied to the global market.

This is the latest in several licenses the U.S. Treasury has issued regarding Russian fuel shipments since the start of the Iran war early this year. But it is the first such license to ease sanctions on diesel for a period lasting longer than the standard 30-day window since the start of the Ukraine war.

The new so-called general license means U.S. sanctions will not apply until April 2027 on deliveries of Russian diesel that has been loaded onto tankers as of Friday. The department extended similar easing of sanctions in March and April even though Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had ruled out such a move earlier in the year.

The extensions continue to underscore how the fallout from the Iran war has boosted Moscow’s ability to profit from its energy exports, which had been restrained by the U.S. and other allies since the invasion of Ukraine.

It's unclear how the move will impact oil prices

"What does this do to prices? I think probably not much,” said Clayton Seigle, an energy strategist and expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

But, Seigle said the new deal is a “great benefit to Russia and to Putin,” who are currently trying to offload their summer-grade diesel for the heavier winter and arctic grades that they will need in the coming months.

“It’s kind of shuffling deck chairs on the Titanic,” said Michael Lynch of the Energy Policy Research Foundation, a non-partisan research institution focused on energy and economics.

“If we get diesel from Russia, basically it means that their existing customers are not going to get it and they’ll have to go somewhere else, and that will keep the price basically where it is now,” Lynch said.

Russia, once a major exporter of diesel, has banned exports since July as it has struggled to meet demand inside the country because of Ukraine’s repeated attacks on Russian oil refineries. The International Energy Agency says Russian diesel output has fallen by about 30%.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told state news agency Tass that Russia is “immediately starting to lift restrictions on diesel exports ahead of schedule.” He said that Moscow could start supplies to the U.S. already in October, and that Russia’s domestic market will be “fully supplied” with diesel, as well.

___

Associated Press writers Will Weissert and Konstantin Toropin in Washington, Alex Veiga in Los Angeles and Farnoush Amiri in New York contributed to this report.

item.title: 美股三大指数集体反弹，市场焦点转向财报季，AI投资热潮面临盈利检验
item.description:
从本周走势来看，美国股市尚未失去上涨动力。尽管周四科技股遭到集中抛售，周五市场仍迅速反弹，而且上涨范围扩展到多个板块。 但市场也显示出明显的脆弱性。 AI企业的高增长预期需要不断得到验证，能源价格上涨可能重新刺激通胀，长期美债收益率维持在5%以上则提高了股票估值面临的门槛。 第三季度财报季因此具有特别重要的意义。如果企业盈利继续大幅超出预期，华尔街可能找到新的理由支持股市上涨，并逐步降低对AI投资情绪的依赖。 反过来，如果盈利增长不及预期，或管理层开始下调未来业绩展望，高估值、高利率与高能源成本叠加形成的压力，也可能让目前的市场反弹难以持续。

item.title: Trump selects Katie Zacharia as next White House press secretary
item.description:
President Donald Trump has selected Katie Zacharia, a conservative commentator who worked briefly at the Department of Homeland Security, as his new press secretary.

Zacharia thanked Trump in a social media post Friday, writing, “Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime.”

In announcing her selection earlier Friday, Trump highlighted her work for Truth Social, the Trump Media & Technology Group and her frequent appearances on Fox and Newsmax.

“She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning,” he added.

Trump in recent days called a number of his close allies and advisers, including former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to seek their opinion of Zacharia, a person familiar with the discussions said. And the president sought Leavitt’s counsel before making a final decision and offering Zacharia the position, they said.

CNN has reached out to Zacharia, who was in the Oval Office with Trump earlier Friday morning, according to a person familiar.

Zacharia’s selection came about quickly. As of last week, she was not being considered for the role, another person familiar said.

Throughout the search to replace Leavitt, the White House struggled with higher-profile names, several of whom had previously criticized Trump. On multiple occasions, senior officials had narrowed down the list, only to find that candidates had said something negative about the president, disqualifying them from the position, according a White House official.

“The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day,” Zacharia wrote on X.

“I look forward to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out,” she said, adding that “following the fabulous Karoline Leavitt is a high standard, and one worth meeting.”

Zacharia’s been a frequent guest on Fox, Newsmax and CNN.

“She’s a friend of most of you,” Trump told reporters while leaving the White House on Friday. “I know she likes people — she likes all of you. Actually, I don’t know if that’s good or bad, but we just hired a new press secretary, and she’s going to be, I think, terrific.”

Zacharia served as a senior communications adviser at the Trump Media and Technology Group and Truth Social since June, which followed a two-month stint as a senior official at the Department of Homeland Security — experiences that Trump also highlighted in his social media post, along with her work in his campaigns.

Zacharia, who has young children and lives in California, commuted back and forth to Washington when she was filling in at DHS. At the time, she told a friend the commute was not sustainable, according to a source familiar with the matter.

Zacharia has also served as a legal adviser for Fix California, a conservative group founded by Trump ally Richard Grenell.

She first came to Washington as an intern for the Republican National Committee during the George W. Bush administration in 2006.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

item.title: Panama hit by magnitude 7.7 and 6.6 earthquakes hours apart, prompting evacuations
item.description:
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck near Panama's southern tip on Friday morning, shaking buildings more than 100 miles away in the capital and prompting evacuations, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. A second powerful 6.6 magnitude earthquake struck the country later in the day following a series of aftershocks.

The initial quake was centered about 7 miles southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba and struck at a depth of about 7 miles, the USGS said. The 6.6 magnitude quake came about two and a half hours later, with its epicenter about 8 miles west of Río Grande on Panama's Pacific coast and a depth of about 6 miles.

The U.S. Pacific Tsunami Warning Center had initially warned about the possibility of tsunami waves hitting Panama's coast, but later said the threat had passed.

Tremors were felt in Panama City, where buildings shook and people evacuated into the streets. Visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news.

"We felt it very strongly. It knocked things over in the kitchen, but we're OK, though we're very scared," Rosendo Domínguez, 60, who is from Herrera province, where the earthquake struck, told The Associated Press by phone. "Everyone is outside, scared."

Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino called for calm on Friday, writing on social media: "What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder."

Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service said on the Telemetro Reporta news channel that damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. He said there were no reports of damage in the capital, which is known for its hundreds of skyscrapers.

Video aired by local news outlets showed a Catholic cathedral collapsing and part of a hotel's facade falling onto a car in the city of Penonomé, in the central province of Coclé. No casualties were immediately reported.

The quake is at least the fourth one this year in Latin America surpassing 7.0 in magnitude, after devastating earthquakes in Venezuela's Guaira in June and a powerful earthquake in western Colombia in August.

Panama lies along the "Ring of Fire," a 25,000-mile arc of volcanoes and fault lines around the Pacific Basin, where most of the world's earthquakes occur.

Panama's Civil Protection said it was investigating possible damage in regions near the epicenter.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/panama-earthquake-tsunami-threat/

item.title: 南中国海争端又起：中菲相互指责南中国海医疗救援事件
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

中菲双方就发生在南中国海有争议海域第二托马斯浅滩附近的一次医疗救助行动相互指责；此外，菲律宾军方报告称，9月份出现在南中国海有争议岛礁周边的中国军舰和海警船数量几乎翻了一番。

据菲律宾军方说，星期四(10月8日)，菲律宾军方需要从第二托马斯浅滩(Second Thomas Shoal，中国称仁爱礁，菲律宾称阿云津礁) 的“马德雷山”号(BRP Sierra Madre)军舰上撤离一名生病的菲律宾军人。

菲律宾海岸警卫队指责中国海警船阻挠紧急撤离行动，其中包括使用高压水炮，显然意在阻止菲律宾巡逻船抵达该浅滩，以接回生病的执勤人员。

菲律宾海岸警卫队发言人、海军少将杰伊·塔里埃拉(Jay Tarriela)表示，这起事件导致任务延误了近10小时，并迫使菲律宾船只出于安全原因撤离，尽管高压水炮并未击中该船。

病人最终在距离第二托马斯浅滩较远的一处汇合点被橡皮艇转移撤离，据报目前病情稳定。

中方提出反驳

中方当日对菲方的说法提出反驳。中方的说法是：8日，菲律宾一艘海警船在未经中方允许的情况下，进入仁爱礁(即第二托马斯浅滩)附近海域，转运中方所说的菲律宾非法“坐滩”军舰的1名伤员。

外交部发言人毛宁9日在例行记者会上表示，中方出于人道主义考虑，允许菲方采取小艇过驳的方式转运伤员，并提供了必要便利。她指责菲方“对中方倒打一耙”，属“挑事生非、哗众取宠”。

菲律宾在第二托马斯浅滩的“马德雷山号”军舰上驻有一支小规模部队。这艘二战时期的老旧军舰由菲律宾1999年故意搁浅在第二托马斯浅滩，以强化其主权主张。菲律宾船只定期向舰上驻军运送食品和其他物资，并轮换人员。第二托马斯浅滩是该地区主要的冲突热点之一。

菲军方：9月份中国军方船只数量较8月份几乎翻倍

与此同时，菲律宾军方在同一日表示，军方9月份在四个南中国海有争议的海域周边，监测到了101艘不同的中国海军和海警船只，而8月和7月的数量分别为56艘和48艘。

菲律宾军方南中国海事务发言人、海军少将罗伊·特立尼达(Roy Vincent Trinidad)告诉法新社，中国增派船只，旨在“摧毁我们国人坚守固有领土的决心”。他将此称为“任务瘫痪”(mission kill)，意在破坏菲方继续执行任务的能力。

近期内中菲冲突不断

最近一段时间以来，中菲双方在南中国海上的冲突不断。菲律宾海岸警卫队10月4日表示，中国船只阻挠了菲方针对一艘涉嫌在南中国海中业岛(菲律宾称帕加萨岛)附近进行炸鱼作业的外国渔船所开展的执法行动。

菲方形容中国海军直升机的出现是一种“不必要的恐吓行为”。

另外，中国科考船“嘉海科7号”9月底、10月初在菲律宾北部巴丹群岛海域徘徊多日，遭菲国海岸警卫队最大舰艇“特蕾莎·马格巴努阿号”(BRP Teresa Magbanua)驱离，在2艘中国海警船伴航下北移吕宋海峡。

中国军方9月27日在南中国海有争议的斯卡伯勒浅滩(Scarborough Shoal, 中国称黄岩岛，菲律宾称马辛洛克浅滩)周边举行了海空联合演训。在此前发生的另一起海上对峙中，中国舰船阻止菲律宾向第二托马斯浅滩执行人员轮换和补给任务

美国重申《美菲共同防御条约》

美国驻菲律宾大使李·利普顿(Lee Lipton)9月26日就中国阻挠菲律宾向第二托马斯浅滩执行补给任务发表声明，谴责中国海警和解放军海军采取“危险的阻挡及其他不负责任的动作”。

他说：“我们与菲律宾盟友站在一起，并赞扬他们表现出的专业和克制。”

利普顿还呼吁中国海警和海军停止使用升级局势的手段。他说，这些行动威胁航行自由以及自由开放的印太地区。

美国多次重申，《美菲共同防御条约》适用于在南中国海任何地点针对菲律宾武装部队、公务船只和飞机发动的武装袭击。

中国声称对南中国海大部分海域拥有主权，其主张与菲律宾及其他几个国家重叠。一个国际仲裁庭2016年裁定，北京广泛海洋主张缺乏法律依据，并认定第二托马斯浅滩位于菲律宾专属经济区内。中国拒绝承认这项裁决。

关键词: 
南中国海
中菲争端
医疗救援事件
中国海警船
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: Isaias was 1 day away from tying a 1905 record for the latest Atlantic hurricane
item.description:
Hurricane Isaias is expected to bring heavy rain, damaging winds and life-threatening storm surge to the northern Gulf Coast when it makes landfall late Friday or early Saturday.

According to the National Hurricane Center, Isaias remains a Category 3 storm with maximum sustained winds of 115 mph, which forecasters consider a "major hurricane."

As of 5 p.m. ET, the storm was located about 90 miles south of Pensacola, Fla., and roughly 125 miles south-southeast of Mobile, Ala., moving north at 17 mph. It is expected to approach the northern Gulf Coast this afternoon and make landfall near the Alabama-Florida state line tonight.

The governors of Florida, Alabama and Georgia have declared states of emergency, along with several Mississippi counties, urging residents to take the first hurricane of an unusually quiet season seriously. Thousands of National Guard soldiers are being deployed.

Is the storm headed your way? Follow it in real time on the new Yahoo Weather app.

Mandatory evacuation orders have been issued for parts of Florida's Walton, Escambia, Okaloosa and Franklin counties. Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey also ordered nonresidents to evacuate Gulf Shores, Orange Beach and Dauphin Island.

Heavy rain and flooding could extend as far north as Tennessee and North Carolina through the weekend. There's also a risk of tornadoes across the Florida Panhandle into southern Georgia.

Follow live updates on Hurricane Isaias below.
